Entertainment We offer a wide range of entertainment to suit every event, from high-energy silent discos and club nights to more relaxed evenings in our pub. selection: Yes Current selection: Yes Current selection: Yes Current selection: Yes The biggest student club night in the capital, your home every single Wednesday night. YOLO has become a cultural phenomenon among Cardiff students, defined by the thousands of VKs sold each week, very creative society socials and of course, staying til' Angels. Y Plas reaches full capacity every week, and our full- building takeovers, YOLOWEEN and SNOLO sell out quicker than you can say '4 VKs for £12'. YOLO FAQs Dress code To keep the vibes high and everyone safe, we have a few ground rules around dress code and what you can bring into the venue. Please note that we reserve the right to confiscate any item that may cause harm or alarm. This includes, but is not limited to: Hi-Vis clothing. Hard Hats. Imitation Weapons such as swords, shields, guns etc. Inflatables. Hand Cuffs – metal or plastic. Anything that may be deemed dangerous by security staff or duty management. Confiscated items will be kept at the security desk until the end of the event. After this time, any items will be disposed of. We are not responsible for any lost or damaged confiscated items. Customers may be refused if items of clothing may cause alarm or distress to others, with no refund given. Inflateable Costumes that may pose a safety risk or impeed others enjoyment will be refused, with no refund given. Large signs, any flags, banners, posters, items, and iPads will be refused. This is to ensure all customers have the best possible view of the event, and to ensure the safety of our customers. Opening hours and contact details Safety in our venues Live music accessibility Accessing our building The Students’ Union building can be accessed from both our Senghennydd Road entrance and our Park Place entrance. If entering from Park Place - Cardiff University has installed a lift at the Park Place entrance to the Students’ Union. You will find this lift next to the entrance to the Centre for Student Life at the bottom of the steps to the Students’ Union. On exiting the lift, please use the automatic door located on the left to enter our Welcome Centre. Once inside the building, we have a lift that will take you to all other floors. If entering from Senghennydd Road, you can use the lift from the Ground Floor to access all other floors in the building. If you have any issues accessing the building, please call our Security Team on 029 2078 1412 . Disabled access at live music events We operate a bookable balcony for all shows for those who have special accessible requirements, however it is operated on a first come, first served basis due to capacity limitations. It is often the case that we are unable to facilitate requests made on the night, but we will always aim to do what we can. Due to capacity restrictions, we can only reserve spaces for 1 user and 1 carer - if your requirements surpass this please let us know. To book a space on the balcony you must FIRST purchase a ticket for the show for yourself, we can then offer you a complimentary carer ticket when requested in advance using the form below. All tickets are subject to availability and capacity. If the balcony is full, we will process a full refund for the ticket purchased so you won't be out of pocket. Please note carers may have a restricted view. Requests must be made via our easy online booking system . Speak to our Customer Service team Email our Customer Service team at [email protected] . Contact Us If you’re having trouble using the website, or require additional information or services not covered here, you can contact our access officer. We aim to respond to all enquiries within 2 working days. For event day enquires, please phone us at: 029 2078 1400 . Each week, on average 8,000 students attend the popular club nights – we are proud that these events are a core part of the Cardiff student experience for a large proportion of the student body. Whilst serious incidents in our clubs are minimal, we are aware that damaging and, on occasion, harmful activity can still occur. We take all reports of inappropriate, harmful and unlawful behaviour incredibly seriously and want to encourage any student who experiences these types of behaviours to report it. Our staff and security team are on hand during events to handle complaints, if you do not feel comfortable reporting at the time, please see the reporting and accessing support section below. Safety Initiatives Cardiff Students’ Union has been working with local partners for many years to deliver other initiatives that will help to safeguard your personal safety at night. These initiatives are available for any Cardiff University student to use: Safety Bus We have partnered with South Wales Police to deliver the Cardiff Safety Bus. The bus patrols the city centre every Wednesday, Friday and Saturday night and will provide help to anyone who needs it. Private Medical Staff During each club night event, we pay for private medically trained staff, with trained paramedics, to be in our venues to support with any medical issues that occur. Where You At app We’re working in partnership with the Where You At app. The app helps you stay connected and find your friends in our venues. You will have access to offline venue maps, friend finding and event information – you can also send pings to notify friends of your location offline. Keep connected and enjoy your night! Download the app Drink Spiking Testing Kits We take the personal safety of our attendees very seriously. Drink spiking with drugs is incredibly uncommon. Spiking by injection is even more uncommon. There has been a significant amount of media exposure contributing to a very real fear. Research however suggests that it is actually very rare. If you believe you have been spiked in our venues, please report to a staff member who will alert the onsite paramedic for assistance. We have invested in drink testing kits to give you immediate testing options at our venues and would encourage any student who is concerned about themselves or a friend at our events to speak to a staff member to access one of these. Please do not be hesitant of taking a spiking test kit in the Union, no action will be taken as a result of a positive test for drugs taken knowingly. Medical staff are employed for your safety. Drink Toppers Drink Toppers & Bottle Stops are available free of charge at all our bars for anyone who wants added drink protection. Please help yourself or ask a member of our bar team. *Shot glasses don't have lids available due to the size of the glass. Security staff We employ a large security team to ensure the safety of attendees at events. This includes several dedicated positions in observational roles to watch for, and act on, inappropriate behaviour. Searches on Entry We conduct random searches as a condition of entry. For occasional events, sniffer dogs are utilised to support the identification of illegal substances. We have a zero-tolerance approach to possession of drugs in our venues, those caught can face a lifetime ban to all events (club nights, gigs and external events) and we may report to the police. Extensive CCTV and Body Cameras We have invested heavily in a CCTV system that has over 300 cameras in operation across our venues. On top of this, many of our security staff will be wearing body cameras to support gaining footage of incidents where required to aide police investigations. Staff Training Programme We’re developing our staff training programme to include information about how to handle inappropriate behaviours and to spot signs of drink tampering. These initiatives are regularly reviewed to understand the effectiveness and we welcome any feedback or improvement suggestions by emailing [email protected] . Student Behaviour Expectations To ensure all our club night and event goers can enjoy themselves in a safe manner, we require all attendees to always behave in an appropriate and respectful manner. If behaviours fall short of our Code of Practice, you will be ejected from the venue and may face a venue exclusion/ban for periods ranging from four weeks to a permanent lifetime ban, we may also pass information about the incident on to the police or to the University complaints procedures. Examples of activity that will not be tolerated in our venues ... And will result in persons being asked to leave the premises and likely to face a ban. Intimidating or abusive behaviour Sexual harrassment Pushing or shoving Violence or aggression of any kind Throwing bottles, cups or vessels, or intentional drinks throwing Horseplay (rough, boisterous behaviour) Failure to comply with a request of staff Possession of illegal substances and/ or spiking of others with illegal substances Possession of any kind of weapon Length of bans and any subsequent action will be determined on a case by case basis depending on the specifics of the incident. However, students and guests attending events are advised that the venue has an absolute zero tolerance to drugs, as well as abusive or aggressive behaviour to any members of staff. Spiking Read our new guidance below, developed in partnership with South-Wales Police. Spiking advice for yourself or a friend Other information about our venues Lost property We experience a large volume of lost property handed in at our venues. Please do take care to look after your belongings and check them into our cloakroom if required. If you have lost an item please visit the Welcome Centre on the 2nd floor of the Students' Union, Cathays or email [email protected] and we will aim to identify and return your property as soon as possible. We aim to keep any lost property for a minimum of 2 weeks from when it is handed in. If you spot a phone, purse or belonging in our venues, please hand into Welcome Centre on the 2nd floor of the Students' Union, Park Place. Queue Management Due to the popularity of our events and our requirement to carry out checks as conditions of entry, you may be required to queue to gain access. Please be respectful of you fellow students and security staff when in queuing lanes. We want to get you to the dance floor as fast as possible! Leaving our venues Please leave our venues in a respectful manner and listen to instructions from security. Reporting and accessing support There are wide-ranging reporting and support services that are in place for students if incidents occur. This can be dependent on the nature of the incident and if you are looking for an investigation to take place or wanting to give feedback on the service or event. Reporting Would you like to report what has happened to South Wales Police? If this is the right option for you, please find ways to contact the police below: You can report anything suspicious, or any situation that makes you concerned about your safety or the safety of others. You can contact South Wales Police on 101 or contact the emergency services on 999 if you think you are in immediate danger. You can also report an incident to South Wales Police online: Email: [email protected] Website: south-wales.police.uk/ If you have experienced any kind of violence, abuse, or unacceptable behaviour and you would like support, we can help. Please find some related support links below. Get urgent advice if you or someone else requires urgent or out of hours support, here's who to contact. Immediate support and safety advice if you have experienced an incident that has caused injury or harm Contacting our Security Team who are patrolling campus and happy to talk to you if you have any security concerns or questions. Protecting yourself and your belongings for tips on personal safety and crime prevention Online safety and your browsing history, protecting emails and passwords? Download our Safezone app to alert Security if you need help or assistance while on campus. If you are off campus the app will alert the police. Violence and abuse resources if you want further information on recognising unhealthy, violent, or abusive behaviours and for further information on consent. Counselling and Wellbeing Support if you need to talk to someone to manage your emotional health and wellbeing. Student Advice if you would like independent and impartial advice Report and Support Report and Support is an online tool to report incidents of violence, abuse, threats, hate crime and mental health concerns to access support. It can also be used by staff and members of the public to report on behalf of or in relation to Cardiff University students. Users can choose to make a report anonymously or give details about themselves. There is also an option to report on behalf of someone else. You can access the Report and Support tool here . Responsibility for responding to and providing support to those who use the Report and Support tool will sit in the Student Support Intervention Team . This new team combines two existing teams: the Disclosure Response team and the Student Intervention team. Close Window Current selection: Yes Current selection: Yes Current selection: Yes Current selection: Yes The Union employs approximately 110 career staff and a further 300 student workers to manage its day-to-day activities. We employ everyone from accountants (Finance), solicitors (Student Advice), to plumbers (Facilities), chefs (Venues) and letting agents (Cardiff Student Letting). Our staff are led by our Chief Executive and a broader Strategic Management Team. Daniel Palmer Chief Executive Daniel became Chief Executive of the Students' Union in June 2013. Daniel is responsible for the day-to-day running of the organisation, oversees the work of the other senior managers and works closely with the Students' Union President and the other sabbatical officers. Daniel helps ensure continuity within the organisation, works closely with senior staff from the University and takes a particular responsibility for the Students' Union’s Finance Team. Daniel serves as the Chief Executive and Managing Director of the Union’s trading company, Cardiff Union Services Limited and reports to the Board of Trustees. Prior to his role at the Students' Union, Daniel has held many senior roles within other students’ unions, most recently as Chief Executive of the University of Portsmouth Students' Union. Raechel Mattey Deputy Chief Executive Raechel joined the Students' Union in June 2018 as the Director of Communications and was later appointed as Deputy Chief Executive in March 2024. Raechel spearheads the enhancement of the organisation's brand, digital presence, and overall influence, aligning efforts with strategic goals. Additionally, she is responsible for driving organisational performance by improving employee practices and enhancing satisfaction levels. Prior to this role, Raechel has held several roles in Students’ Unions and the National Union of Students, most recently as Deputy CEO at Middlesex University Students’ Union. Raechel oversees Marketing and Web, People and Governance, Student Voice and Advice teams, as well as being the senior lead for the complaints policy across the organisation. Steve Wilford Director of Participation & Safeguarding Steve has worked for the Students' Union since April 2008, becoming the Director of Membership Services in September 2013. Steve is responsible for the Union’s Membership Services and student activities, including Student Advice, Sport, Societies, Volunteering, Student Media, Jobshop, Training & Development and Student Voice. Steve is also the senior manager responsible for coordinating the Union’s democratic activities including elections and administration of Student Senate. In Summer 2017, Steve's job title changed to Director of Engagement & Participation, to better reflect the language used within the organisation. Phil Dayment Director of Enterprise Phil joined the Students' Union in 2015 as Food and Beverage Manager, advancing to Head of Venues in 2016, a position he held until November 2023, when he assumed the role of Director of Enterprise. As Director of Enterprise, Phil leads the organisation's commercial income-generating areas and oversees financial performance. A key aspect of his role is to ensure the highest possible student experiences and satisfaction with the services he oversees, thereby ensuring that the Cardiff experience is of the highest quality. Before this role, Phil accumulated 16 years of experience in the hospitality sector, ranging from General Manager to Regional Wide Cluster Group Management. His experience spans late-night bars and clubs, hotels, and restaurants across the UK. Phil oversees the Venues Department, Cardiff Student Letting, Sales, and Customer Service. Jan Boyce Director of Finance Jan joined the Students' Union in November 2021 and as Director of Finance, leads the strategic management of its financial resources, ensuring long term sustainability and operational efficiency. With a strong track record in senior financial leadership roles across both charitable and commercial sectors, Jan brings a wealth of expertise in financial planning, governance, and risk management. She holds a degree in Mathematics from Cardiff University and is a Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England & Wales. A qualification she gained whilst working for PwC Cardiff. Mae'r Undeb yn cyflogi tua 110 o staff gyrfa a 300 o fyfyrwyr i reoli ei weithgareddau o ddydd i ddydd. Rydym yn cyflogi pawb o gyfrifwyr (Cyllid), a chyfreithwyr (Cyngor i Fyfyrwyr), i blymwyr (Cyfleusterau), cogyddion (Lleoliadau) ac asiantau gosod eiddo (Gosod Tai Myfyrwyr Caerdydd). Mae ein staff wedi’u harwain gan ein Prif Weithredwr a Thîm Rheoli Strategol ehangach. Daniel Palmer Prif Weithredwr Daeth Daniel yn Brif Weithredwr Undeb y Myfyrwyr ym mis Mehefin 2013. Mae Daniel yn gyfrifol am redeg y sefydliad o ddydd i ddydd, goruchwylio gwaith yr uwch reolwyr eraill, a gweithio'n agos gyda Llywydd Undeb y Myfyrwyr a'r swyddogion sabothol eraill. Mae Daniel yn helpu i sicrhau parhad o fewn y sefydliad, gan weithio'n agos gydag uwch staff o'r Brifysgol a chymryd cyfrifoldeb penodol dros Dîm Cyllid Undeb y Myfyrwyr. Mae Daniel yn gwasanaethu fel Prif Weithredwr a Rheolwr Gyfarwyddwr cwmni masnachu’r Undeb, Gwasanaethau Undeb Caerdydd Cyfyngedig, ac mae'n atebol i’r Bwrdd Ymddiriedolwyr. Cyn ei rôl yn Undeb y Myfyrwyr, gwnaeth Daniel weithio mewn sawl uwch rôl o fewn undebau myfyrwyr eraill, yn fwyaf diweddar fel Prif Weithredwr Undeb Myfyrwyr Prifysgol Portsmouth. Raechel Mattey Dirprwy Brif Weithredwr Ymunodd Raechel ag Undeb y Myfyrwyr ym mis Mehefin 2018 fel y Cyfarwyddwr Cyfathrebu ac fe'i penodwyd yn Ddirprwy Brif Weithredwr ym mis Mawrth 2024. Mae Raechel yn arwain y gwaith o wella brand, presenoldeb digidol, a dylanwad cyffredinol y sefydliad, gan alinio ymdrechion â nodau strategol. Yn ogystal, mae'n gyfrifol am yrru perfformiad sefydliadol trwy wella arferion gweithio a lefelau boddhad. Cyn y rôl hon, gweithiodd Raechel mewn sawl rôl mewn Undebau Myfyrwyr ac Undeb Cenedlaethol y Myfyrwyr, yn fwyaf diweddar fel Dirprwy Brif Swyddog Gweithredol Undeb Myfyrwyr Prifysgol Middlesex. Mae Raechel yn goruchwylio timau Marchnata a'r We, Pobl a Llywodraethiant, Llais Myfyrwyr a Chyngor, yn ogystal â bod yn uwch arweinydd ar gyfer y polisi cwynion ar draws y sefydliad. Steve Wilford Cyfarwyddwr Cyfranogiad a Diogelu Mae Steve wedi gweithio i Undeb y Myfyrwyr ers Ebrill 2008, gan ddod yn Gyfarwyddwr Gwasanaethau Aelodaeth ym mis Medi 2013. Mae Steve yn gyfrifol am Wasanaethau Aelodaeth yr Undeb a gweithgareddau myfyrwyr, gan gynnwys Cyngor i Fyfyrwyr, Chwaraeon, Cymdeithasau, Gwirfoddoli, Cyfryngau Myfyrwyr, y Siop Swyddi, Hyfforddiant & Datblygu, a Llais y Myfyriwr. Steve yw hefyd yr uwch reolwr sy'n gyfrifol am gydlynu gweithgareddau democrataidd yr Undeb gan gynnwys etholiadau a gweinyddiaeth Senedd y Myfyrwyr. Yn Haf 2017, newidiodd teitl swydd Steve i Gyfarwyddwr Ymgysylltu a Chyfranogiad, er mwyn adlewyrchu'r iaith a ddefnyddir o fewn y sefydliad yn well. Phil Dayment Cyfarwyddwr Menter Ymunodd Phil ag Undeb y Myfyrwyr yn 2015 fel Rheolwr Bwyd a Diod, gan symud i fod yn Bennaeth Lleoliadau yn 2016, swydd a ddaliodd tan fis Tachwedd 2023, pan gymerodd rôl Cyfarwyddwr Menter. Fel Cyfarwyddwr Menter, mae Phil yn arwain meysydd cynhyrchu-incwm masnachol y sefydliad ac yn goruchwylio perfformiad ariannol. Agwedd allweddol o’i rôl yw sicrhau’r profiadau myfyrwyr gorau posibl a boddhad gyda'r gwasanaethau y mae'n eu goruchwylio, a thrwy hynny sicrhau bod profiadau myfyrwyr yng Nghaerdydd o'r ansawdd uchaf. Cyn y rôl hon, gweithiodd Phil yn y sector lletygarwch am 16 mlynedd, mewn rolau amrywiol o Reolwr Cyffredinol i Reolwr Grŵp Clwstwr Rhanbarthol. Mae ei brofiad yn cynnwys bariau, clybiau, gwestai a bwytai ledled y DU. Mae Phil yn goruchwylio'r Adran Lleoliadau, Gosod Tai Myfyrwyr Caerdydd, yr Adran Gwerthu a Gwasanaeth Cwsmeriaid. Jan Boyce Cyfarwyddwr Cyllid Ymunodd Jan ag Undeb y Myfyrwyr ym mis Tachwedd 2021, ac fel Cyfarwyddwr Cyllid, mae'n arwain rheolaeth strategol ein hadnoddau ariannol, gan sicrhau cynaladwyedd hirdymor ac effeithlonrwydd gweithredol. Gyda hanes cryf mewn rolau arweinyddiaeth ariannol uwch ar draws y sectorau elusennol a masnachol, mae Jan yn dod â chyfoeth o arbenigedd mewn cynllunio cyllidol, llywodraethiant a rheoli risg. Mae ganddi radd mewn Mathemateg o Brifysgol Caerdydd ac mae'n Gymrawd Sefydliad Cyfrifwyr Siartredig Cymru a Lloegr. Cymhwyster a enillodd wrth weithio i PwC Caerdydd. Close Window Current selection: Yes Current selection: Yes Current selection: Yes Current selection: Yes Spanning both the Cathays and Heath Park campuses, the purpose-built SU building operates 24-hours a day and houses cafes, shops, bars, music venues, a letting agency and study spaces for students to make the most of their time at University. Our address Cardiff Students' Union Park Place Cardiff CF10 3QN Getting here By road Cardiff is served by the M4 and is easily accessible from all parts of the UK. From the southwest, take the M5 and from the south of England, follow major A roads to the M4. From Scotland, the north of England and the Midlands, travel via the M50 to the M4. Travelling east on the M4. Leave the motorway at Junction 32, follow the A470, signposted City Centre, into the Cathays area of the city. Travelling west on the M4. Leave the motorway at Junction 29, follow the A48(M)/A48, signposted Cardiff East and South, to the A470. Follow the A470, signposted City Centre, into the Cathays area of the city. By rail High speed inter-city trains provide frequent services between all major UK cities. The Cardiff-London service, from London Paddington, runs regularly throughout the day. Frequent services also connect Cardiff with Bristol, Birmingham, Southampton, Manchester, Liverpool and with many other cities and towns. From Cardiff Central Station there is a frequent train service which stops at Cathays Station, next to the Students' Union. Visit the Transport for Wales website for further information. By bus Visit Cardiff Bus to plan your journey by bus within Cardiff. If you’re travelling to Cardiff via bus from outside of the city, National Express and Megabus offer services that run regularly. Accessibility We want all visitors to our building to feel welcome when they visit us. Accessing our building The Students’ Union building can be accessed from both our Senghennydd Road entrance and our Park Place entrance. If entering from Park Place - Cardiff University has installed a lift at the Park Place entrance to the Students’ Union. You will find this lift next to the entrance to the Centre for Student Life at the bottom of the steps to the Students’ Union. On exiting the lift, please use the automatic door located on the left to enter our Welcome Centre. Once inside the building, we have a lift that will take you to all other floors. If entering from Senghennydd Road, you can use the lift from the Ground Floor to access all other floors in the building. If you have any issues accessing the building, please call our Security Team on 029 2078 1412 . Senghenydd Road entrance and exit is closed from 11pm to 7am every day. During these hours, you will not be able to use the building as a through route. Park Place entrance is accessible to students 24/7. Between 11pm-7am, please ring the bell at the doors for entry. Students will be required to show ID cards to use the student lounge after 11pm and over weekends. At times during some large-scale events, there may be additional restrictions. Disabled access at live music events We operate a bookable balcony for all shows for those who have special accessible requirements, however it is operated on a first come, first served basis due to capacity limitations. It is often the case that we are unable to facilitate requests made on the night, but we will always aim to do what we can. Due to capacity restrictions, we can only reserve spaces for 1 user and 1 carer - if your requirements surpass this please let us know. To book a space on the balcony you must FIRST purchase a ticket for the show for yourself, we can then offer you a complimentary carer ticket when requested in advance using the form below. All tickets are subject to availability and capacity. If the balcony is full, we will process a full refund for the ticket purchased so you won't be out of pocket. Please note carers may have a restricted view. Requests must be made via our easy online booking system . Baby changing facilities Baby-changing facilities are available throughout the building. Please see below the list of available facilities. Ground floor – Accessible WC (near Co-op) First Floor Level 1 - Accessible WC Second Floor - Great Hall Balcony Accessible WC Third Floor - Accessible WC Fourth floor – Accessible WC To access baby-changing facilities, please speak to the Welcome Centre team on the second floor. Speak to our Customer Service team Email our Customer Service team at [email protected] . O’r de-orllewin, dilynwch yr M5 cyn defnyddio heolydd A i gyrraedd yr M4. O’r Alban, a gogledd a chanolbarth Lloegr, teithiwch ar hyd yr M50 i’r M4. Wrth deithio tua’r dwyrain ar yr M4, gadewch y draffordd ar gyffordd 32, a dilynwch yr A470, gydag arwyddion Canol y Ddinas, at ardal Cathays. Wrth deithio tua’r gorllewin ar yr M4, gadewch y draffordd ar gyffordd 29, gan ddilyn yr A48(M)/A48 ac arwyddion Dwyrain a Gogledd Caerdydd, tan i chi gyrraedd yr A470. Mae gwasanaeth Caerdydd-Llundain yn rhedeg yn gyson trwy gydol y dydd. Mae gwasanaethau cyson hefyd yn cysylltu Caerdydd â Bryste, Birmingham, Southampton, Manceinion, Lerpwl, a sawl dinas a thref arall. O Orsaf Caerdydd Canolog mae gwasanaeth rheolaidd i Orsaf Cathays, gerllaw Undeb y Myfyrwyr. Ewch i wefan Trafnidiaeth Cymru am ragor o wybodaeth. Bws Ewch i Fws Caerdydd i gynllunio eich siwrnai bws o fewn Caerdydd. Os yn teithio i Gaerdydd ar fws o ddinas arall, mae’r National Express a Megabus yn cynnig gwasanaethau rheolaidd. Hygyrchedd Rydym am i bob ymwelydd i’n hadeilad deimlo wedi’u croesawu. Mynediad i’n hadeilad Mae modd cael mynediad at adeilad Undeb y Myfyrwyr o Heol Senghennydd a Phlas y Parc. Os yn defnyddio mynedfa Plas y Parc gallwch ddefnyddio lifft Prifysgol Caerdydd. Mae’r lifft ger troed y grisiau at Undeb y Myfyrwyr. Wedi i chi adael y lifft, defnyddiwch y drws awtomatig wedi’i leoli ar ochr chwith ein Canolfan Groeso. Unwaith yn yr adeilad, gallwch gymryd lifft i loriau eraill. Os yn defnyddio mynedfa Heol Senghennydd, gallwch ddefnyddio’r lifft ar y llawr gwaelod i gyrraedd pob llawr o’r adeilad. Os gewch unrhyw broblemau wrth gael mynediad at yr adeilad cysylltwch â’r Tîm Diogelwch ar 029 2078 1412 . Mae mynedfa ac allanfa Ffordd Senghennydd ar gau o 11yh i 7yb bob dydd. Yn ystod yr oriau hyn, ni fyddwch yn gallu defnyddio'r adeilad fel llwybr i gerdded drwodd. Mae mynedfa Plas y Parc ar gael i fyfyrwyr 24/7. Rhwng 11yh-7yb, canwch y gloch wrth y drysau i gael mynediad. Bydd gofyn i fyfyrwyr ddangos cerdyn adnabod i ddefnyddio Lolfa'r Myfyrwyr (3ydd llawr) ar ôl 11yh a thros benwythnosau. Ar adegau yn ystod rhai digwyddiadau graddfa fawr, efallai y bydd cyfyngiadau ychwanegol. Mynediad anabl at ddigwyddiadau cerddoriaeth fyw Mae gennym ardal balconi y mae modd ei archebu ar gyfer rheiny ag anghenion hygyrchedd ychwanegol. Caiff y system archebu ei weithredu ar sail gyntaf i’r felin o ganlyniad i gyfyngiadau capasiti. Yn aml, ni allwn gyflawni ceisiadau sy’n cael eu gwneud ar y noson, ond byddwn bob tro yn ceisio eich helpu os fydd modd. O ganlyniad i gyfyngiadau capasiti gallwn ond gadw lle ar gyfer 1 defnyddiwr ac 1 gofalwr – os oes angen mwy o gymorth arnoch rhowch wybod i ni. I archebu lle ar y balconi rhaid i chi archebu tocyn i’r sioe YN GYNTAF, wedyn gallwn gynnig tocyn gofalwr am ddim wedi i’r ffurflen isod cael ei chwblhau. Mae pob tocyn yn ddibynnol ar argaeledd a chapasiti. Os yw’r balconi yn llawn, byddwn yn darparu ad-daliad llawn ar gyfer y tocyn gwnaethoch archebu. Nodwch, efallai y bydd gallu gofalwyr i weld y llwyfan wedi’i gyfyngu ychydig. Rhaid gwneud ceisiadau trwy ein system archebu syml . Close Window Current selection: Yes Current selection: Yes Current selection: Yes Current selection: Yes Cardiff Students’ Union provides a range of advertising opportunities
to help you promote your business directly to the Cardiff University
student market. Whether you're looking for digital solutions or want to come on campus to speak to students in person, we can help you access this vibrant audience. Media Packs Click on the images below to find out more about what we offer. To discuss a booking, contact one of our friendly sales team at [email protected] or call on 029 2078 1487. Booking Process Our booking process is geared towards helping you find the advertising solution that best suits your needs. Our team are on hand at each stage to help you, just get in touch at [email protected] or call on 029 2078 1487. " What a great event yesterday was! It was a fantastic opportunity to promote our
brand as many students we spoke to weren’t aware of Glamorgan Cricket and its
location. We would be really interested in any similar events you may have in the
future that we could get involved in. Glamorgan Cricket, Refreshers’ Fair 2023 Frequently Asked Questions Making a booking What media do you offer? View our Freshers' media pack Do you offer bespoke packages? Yes, we are always working closely with our clients to create packages that best represent their campaign. Please contact us to discuss this further. How do I go ahead with a booking? Check out our booking process above. Cancellation I have made a booking, can I cancel? Please refer to the cancellation policy in our Terms & Conditions . When does payment need to be made? Payment needs to be made within 30 days of invoice or before the live date of activation / media whichever is first. Can I pay via invoice? Yes, you can pay via invoice. If you have not worked with us before, you will be required to complete the new customer section on our online booking form for us to add you to our finance invoicing system. Can I pay via card? Yes, this is no problem. Please let the sales team know that you would like to pay with card so that we can arrange this for you. Card payments can be processed over the phone prior to the event. You are also welcome to pop into the students’ Union to pay via card. Do you offer discount for charities & local businesses? If you are a registered charity, we will offer you 50% off the listed prices on the media pack. We have a limited number of Charity Freshers’ fair stalls, please see Freshers’ prices for details on this. Please get in touch to discuss this. Media assets What are the artwork specs? View our media dimensions and specifications here . What is the deadline to send media assets? We require media assets at least 1 week prior to the live date. Anything after this may result in cancellation or movement of the live date. My artwork is not going to be ready in time for the agreed deadline date. We know that sometimes things get in the way due to unforeseen circumstances, which may cause a delay in artwork being finalised. Please contact us as soon as possible so we can work something out with you. If this is less than 1 week before the live date, we cannot guarantee we will be able to reschedule. What if I am late sending the media assets? It is your responsibility to ensure assets are sent over in the correct format on time. Any assets we have not received will be considered ‘missed’ and will be non-refundable If you know that you will not reach the deadline, please contact us as soon as possible. View our media dimensions and specifications here . Will you provide evidence that our advert is live? Absolutely, we will send over either photos or screenshots of any adverts that are live so that you can see them live. On-Site Stalls What time can I arrive? Please confirm these details with the sales team. Is there Parking? There is no onsite parking available at Cardiff Students’ Union as we are a city centre location. However, there are several short and long stay public car parks located nearby. There is also on street parking available in the vicinity with parking meters. SMARTMAP - You can check where there are free spaces by downloading the smartmap app. Is there a train station nearby? The nearest train station is Cathays (Cardiff) – next to Cardiff Students’ Union site. How do I find you? Cardiff Students’ Union Park Place Cardiff CF10 3QN If you are using our service tunnel, please follow directions to postcode CF24 4AG. The service tunnel is in between Cardiff Uni Sport and Abacws building. Head to the Welcome Centre on the 2nd floor to sign in. Are there any vehicle height restrictions? Please get in touch if you are worried about vehicle height restrictions. There are two ways of getting to Senghennydd road. One way means you will come across a bridge with a Bridge height restriction 14.3 meters. Is there Wi-Fi available Yes, we have Wi-Fi. You will be provided with instructions on how to connect on the day. However, we cannot be responsible should there be a problem with connection on the day. Will I have access to power? Please let us know in advance of your activation date so that we can accommodate you. CSU reserves the right to disconnect stallholders from the power supply at any time. Notice of this will be given subject to health and safety requirements.
If you have booked a Freshers’ or Refreshers Fair stall, please note that power is not guaranteed. What is provided in a standard stall? 3x2m trestle table and 2 chairs. Access to power and Wi-Fi. What day has the highest footfall? We can’t guarantee footfall on the day of your event. However, please get in touch and we can advise the best day / time of year to visit. Do you have a service tunnel to unload our goods? Yes, please arrange with us prior to arrival if you require use of the service tunnel so that we can let our security team know. Please use the following postcode to access Senghennydd Road (Rear of the building). This is where you can access our service tunnel if you have been allocated a loading bay slot – CF24 4AG. Can I have our promotional material delivered to Cardiff Students’ Union prior to the event? No. Unfortunately, we are unable to accept deliveries or store anything due to our limited storage space. Can I leave anything overnight? No. Unfortunately, we are unable to store anything overnight due to our limited storage and evening activity. Can food be handed out at the stall? Any companies providing ‘food’ samples are to complete a Food Hygiene Disclaimer Notice – please contact [email protected] prior to arrival. Can alcohol be distributed? Alcohol samples need to be approved by a member of the sales team. We cannot allow samples to be handed out that have not been approved by Cardiff Students' Union. Please get in touch to discuss this with a member of the team. Who is my contact on the day of the stall? Please report to welcome centre on 2nd floor of the SU when you arrive. Your contact will be the sales & customer service team, [email protected] . Ydyn, rydym o hyd yn gweithio’n agos gyda chleientiaid i greu pecynnau sy’n cynrychioli eu hymgyrchoedd orau. Cysylltwch â ni i drafod hyn ymhellach. Sut ydw i’n gwneud archeb? Gweler ein proses archebu uchod. Canslo Rydw i wedi gwneud archeb, ga’ i ganslo? Gweler y polisi canslo yn ein Telerau & Amodau . Pryd mae’n rhaid talu? Rhaid talu o fewn 30 diwrnod i’r anfoneb neu cyn i unrhyw gyfryngau cael eu cyhoeddi – pa bynnag un sydd gyntaf. A allaf dalu trwy anfoneb? Gallwch, gallwch dalu trwy anfoneb. Os nad ydych wedi gweithio gyda ni o’r blaen rhaid i chi gwblhau’r adran cwsmer newydd ar ein ffurflen archebu ar-lein er mwyn i ni eich ychwanegu at ein system anfonebu. A allaf dalu â charden? Gallwch, nid yw hyn yn broblem. Gadewch i’r tîm gwerthu wybod hoffech dalu â charden, fel eu bod yn gallu trefnu hyn i chi. Gellir prosesu taliadau carden dros y ffôn cyn y digwyddiad. Mae yna hefyd groeso i chi alw heibio i Undeb y Myfyrwyr er mwyn talu â charden. Ydych chi’n cynnig disgownt i elusennau & busnesau lleol? Os ydych yn elusen gofrestredig, byddwn yn cynnig 50% oddi ar bris arferol pecynnau cyfryngau. Mae gennym nifer cyfyngedig o stondinau ar gyfer elusennau yn ffeiriau’r Glas - gweler prisiau’r Glas am fanylion hyn. Cysylltwch â ni i drafod mwy. Manyleb cyfryngau Beth yw’r canllawiau ar gyfer deunydd cyfryngau? Gweler ein dimensiynau a manylebau cyfryngau yma . Erbyn pryd mae’n rhaid danfon deunydd cyfryngau? Mae angen asedau cyfryngau arnom 1 wythnos cyn iddynt fynd yn fyw. Gall unrhyw beth wedi’i ddanfon wedi hyn arwain at ganslo neu symud trefniadau. Ni fydd fy neunydd yn barod erbyn y terfyn amser a gytunwyd. Rydym yn deall y gall amgylchiadau annisgwyl achosi oedi. Cysylltwch â ni cyn gynted â phosib er mwyn i ni geisio aildrefnu neu ddarganfod datrysiad. Os fydd hyn yn digwydd llai nag 1 wythnos cyn y dyddiad byw, ni allwn gadarnhau y bydd modd aildrefnu. Beth os fyddaf yn anfon deunydd cyfryngau yn hwyr? Eich cyfrifoldeb chi yw sicrhau bod asedau’n cael eu hanfon yn y fformat cywir ac ar amser. Bydd unrhyw asedau nad sy’n cael eu derbyn wedi’u hystyried ‘ar goll’ ac ni fydd modd gwneud ad-daliad o ganlyniad i hyn. Os ydych yn gwybod na fydd modd cyrraedd y terfyn amser cysylltwch â ni cyn gynted â phosib. Gweler ein dimensiynau a manylebau cyfryngau yma . A fyddwch yn darparu tystiolaeth bod ein hysbyseb yn fyw? Wrth gwrs, byddwn yn anfon llun neu sgrin-lun o unrhyw hysbysebion sy’n fyw, fel eich bod yn gallu eu gweld. Stondinau ar y safle Pa amser allaf gyrraedd? Cadarnhewch y manylion yma gyda’r tîm gwerthu. Oes parcio? Nid oes unrhyw parcio ar gael ar safle Undeb Myfyrwyr Caerdydd gan ein bod yng nghanol y ddinas. Ond mae yna sawl maes parcio cyhoeddus arhosiad byr a hir gerllaw. Mae yna hefyd parcio ar y stryd – rhaid talu am hyn. SMARTMAP - Gallwch weld gwagleoedd ar ap Smartmap. Oes gorsaf drên gerllaw? Yr orsaf drên agosaf yw Cathays (Caerdydd) – ar bwys safle Undeb Myfyrwyr Caerdydd. Sut ydw i'n dod o hyd i chi? Undeb Myfyrwyr Caerdydd Plas y Parc Caerdydd CF10 3QN Os ydych yn defnyddio ein twnnel gwasanaethau dilynwch gyfeiriadau i’r cod post CF24 4AG. Mae’r twnnel gwasanaethau rhwng adeilad Chwaraeon Prifysgol Caerdydd ac adeilad Abacws. Dewch i’r Ganolfan Groeso ar yr 2il lawr i gofrestru. Oes unrhyw gyfyngiadau i daldra cerbydau? Cysylltwch â ni os ydych yn pryderu am gyfyngiadau taldra. Mae yna dwy ffordd o gyrraedd Heol Senghennydd. Mae un ffordd yn golygu y bydd rhaid mynd o dan bont gyda chyfyngiad taldra o 14.3 metr. Oes Wi-Fi ar gael? Oes, mae gennym Wi-Fi. Byddwn yn eich darparu â chyfarwyddiadau am sut i gysylltu iddo ar y dydd. Ond, ni fyddwn yn gyfrifol os fydd problem wrth gysylltu ar y dydd. A fydd gennyf fynediad at bŵer? Rhowch wybod o flaen llaw am eich anghenion fel ein bod yn gallu darparu ar eich cyfer. Mae UMC yn cadw’r hawl i ddatgysylltu stondinau o’r pŵer ar unrhyw adeg. Byddwn yn rhoi rhybudd am hyn yn ddibynnol ar anghenion iechyd a diogelwch. Nid yw pŵer wedi’i warantu. Beth sydd wedi’i ddarparu gyda stondin arferol? Bwrdd 3x2m a 2 cadair. Pa ddiwrnod sy’n gweld y nifer mwyaf o fyfyrwyr yn mynychu? Ni allwn warantu faint o bobl fydd yn mynychu ar ddiwrnod eich digwydd. Ond, os gysylltwch â ni, gallwn gynghori am y diwrnod/amser y flwyddyn gorau i ymweld. Oes gennych dwnnel gwasanaethau i ni allu dadlwytho cynnyrch? Oes, trefnwch â ni ymlaen llaw os oes angen i chi ddefnyddio’r twnnel, fel ein bod yn gallu rhoi gwybod i’n tîm diogelwch. Defnyddiwch y cod post canlynol am fynediad at Heol Senghennydd (cefn yr adeilad). Dyma le gallwch gael mynediad at y twnnel os ydym wedi dyrannu bae dadlwytho i chi – CF24 4AG. A allaf adael unrhyw beth dros nos? Na. Yn anffodus ni allwn storio unrhyw beth dros nos o ganlyniad i gyfyngiadau ein storfeydd a gweithgareddau gyda’r nos. A oes modd dosbarthu bwyd o’r stondin? Last year over 22,000 students attended our fair over the five days. Are all students invited the the Freshers’ fair? Yes, all Cardiff University students can attend the Freshers’ fair subject to building capacity. Booking details Can I reserve a particular stall location? The stalls are allocated by the sales team in advance of the fair. Stalls are allocated by the sales team before the fair. We cannot guarantee specific locations, but we consider your preferences from the Freshers booking form to plan the layout and optimise the experience for both exhibitors and students. I have booked a standard stall – How big will the stall be and what is included? Standard stall spaces are 3m x 2m Includes: 1 table and 2 chairs, queue management must be within your allocated space Wi-Fi access (details in your welcome pack on arrival), power is on a first-come, first-served We will NOT be providing backing boards – companies are advised to bring their own roller banners / backing displays. I have booked a premium stall – How big will the stall be and what is included? Premium stall spaces are 5m x 4m 1 Table and 2 chairs will be provided, dedicated queuing space outside your stall & priority access to a service tunnel slot Wi-Fi access (details in your welcome pack on arrival) Access to power We will NOT be providing backing boards – companies are advised to bring their own roller banners / backing displays. On the day Where can I unload for Fairs? Priority access is given to premium stallholders. If you wish to use our service tunnel to unload, please agree a loading bay time slot with the sales team prior to your arrival to avoid congestion. Please use the following postcode to access Senghennydd Road (rear of the building) This is where you can access our service tunnel if you have been allocated a loading bay slot – CF24 4AG. We are attending more than one day of the Freshers’ fair; do we need to take down our stalls? Unless told otherwise, we cannot store anything overnight and you will be required to take down and set up again each day due to other Freshers’ events happening throughout the week. How many staff members can I bring along on the day? Due to venue capacity, we allow up to 4 representatives per stall at any one time. We would be happy if you would like staff members to swap throughout the day. Can food be handed out at the stall? Any companies providing ‘food’ samples are to complete a Food Hygiene Disclaimer Notice – please contact [email protected] prior to arrival. Can alcohol be handed out at the stall? Alcohol samples require prior approval from the sales team. You must complete and return the alcohol distribution form and follow our alcohol sampling policy. Contact [email protected] to discuss. Is there any promotional material we are not allowed to hand out on the day? All activity must be declared to the Sales team via the information form prior to the event.
The following items are prohibited and will not be allowed at the fair: Promotion or giveaway of pizza. Any glass. The Union’s activities are managed within a group of companies; the parent charitable company is called Cardiff University Students’ Union (CUSU), and CUSU has a wholly owned subsidiary called Cardiff Union Services Limited (CUSL). Corporate Structure Each company in the group is a separate legal entity with its own Board. You can find out more about the responsibilities and remits of these Boards below Cardiff Students' Union Board of Trustees The Board is responsible for ensuring the effective day-to-day management of the Union, setting long-term goals, setting operational policies, and managing risks. The Board has ultimate responsibility for directing the affairs of the organisation, ensuring that it is well-run and delivering its charitable objectives. Meet the trustees Board Committees To help with decision making, the Students' Union Board of Trustees has five Committees which have delegated authority for specific areas of organisational activity. Finance And Risk Committee People, Diversity, Inclusion and Safety Committee Satisfaction, Engagement and Participation Committee Chief Executive's Appraisal Group Appointments & Renumeration Committee Cardiff Union Services Limited (CUSL), Board of Directors CUSL exists to promote the social and educational welfare of the students at Cardiff University by providing services and facilities to its students. Any profits made by CUSL are gifted to CUSU in pursuit of the Union’s charitable objectives. CUSL has an independent Board of Directors that oversee the work of the company, ensure that it is meeting its objectives and are ultimately responsible for it. Maria Pollard, Students’ Union President, is the Chair of CUSL Board and Daniel Palmer (CEO) is the Managing Director. Trustees The Board comprises 15 members and meets at least four times a year to carry out its
business. Trustees are appointed according to the rules laid out in the Union’s Articles of
Association, with students directly electing the seven Sabbatical Trustees via the annual elections in
February / March every year. What the trustees do Trustees provide regular reports on their activities to the Union’s Student Senate, with
Sabbatical Trustees being held being further accountable via the Student Senate Scrutiny
Committee. The Board has ultimate responsibility, individually, and collectively, for directing the
affairs of
the organisation, ensuring that it is well-run and delivering its charitable objectives. Sabbatical Trustees The Sabbatical Trustees are the seven annually elected sabbatical officers
who
act as the Union's primary student representatives and who take on specifica portfolios of
responsilibity. Sabbatical officers are paid employees who take a year out of their studies or carry out
the
role after completion of their final year. The SU President is a Sabbatical Trustee and oversees the
work of
the other sabbatical officers. The SU President is the ex officio Chair of the Board. Student Trustees The Student Trustees are three studying students who undertake the role on a voluntary basis
whilst
completing their studies and can serve for up to two years. Students are invited to apply to be
Student Trustees as and when vacancies arise and are nominated based on their knowledge, skills,
and
experience. Apply to be a trustee University Nominated Trustees The two University Nominated Trustees are nominated by the University Council, with at least
one of
them being a serving member of the University Council. The University Nominated Trustees bring
professional skills to the Board as well as an excellent understanding of Cardiff University.
University Nominated Trustees undertake the role on a voluntary basis for four years and can
serve a
maximum of four terms. External Trustees The three External Trustees are nominated by the Board based on their professional knowledge,
skills and experience they can bring to the Board. External Trustees undertake the role on a
voluntary basis and often take on additional responsibilities within the sub-committees of the

An award-winning organisation 2nd Place in the WhatUni Student Choice Awards 2022-2025 for Best Students’ Union 1* accreditation and ranked 56th in the Sunday Times Top 100 Best Not-for-Profit organisations 2020, and 21st in the UK for Education and Training 2021 Top 30 Best Companies to Work For in Wales 2020 Investors in Diversity Stage 3 and ranked 65th in the National Centre for Diversity (NCFC) Top 100 index 2020 What we offer our staff We spend a lot of our time helping our students become the most awesome version of themselves , so it makes sense that we do the same for our hard-working staff. When you join our career staff team you’ll get access to all the great benefits below, so if you’re looking for a job that is more than just a paycheck, the SU might just be your perfect fit. What you'll get from us Helping you develop We make sure that everyone has a personal development plan to develop their skills, give them access to training and qualifications, and to learn from people within their field. Setting goals We also get our staff to set themselves challenging objectives to help them achieve the things they want to through their role. Work/life balance We understand that some people need a flexible approach to their working hours. We will consider offering a range of flexible working options that fit with your life commitments. Taking care of your retirement Staff* are automatically enrolled into the NEST Government Pension Scheme. We also offer a scheme with Royal London Pensions, to which the company contributes 4%. *staff over 22 and who earn over £10,000 Extra perks Party time! Throughout the year, we have plenty of activities for staff to take part in, as well as our annual Christmas party and quarterly staff socials. Special offers and discounts Enjoy a whopping 50% off food and drink in our 'Proud to Serve' Starbucks outlet and pub. That morning coffee or lunchtime bite just got a whole lot tastier. Stay fit, stay happy Forget expensive gym memberships, we have a private staff-only gym that you can use for free! Time to unwind We offer free spa passes to staff for those moments when you need to decompress and enjoy a little pampering. Giving something back We encourage our staff to give something back through volunteering and we will support you in developing yourself outside of your day-to-day job. Equality, diversity & inclusion As an employer, we want to attract a diverse and varied workforce who live and breathe our inclusive values, and who treat themselves, each other, and our students with dignity and respect. Our services should always be available on a non-discriminatory basis, and the SU should be a safe, supportive and welcoming environment for students, staff and visitors. How do we do that? The right systems We have an Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Policy that lays out what we need to know as employees. It also clarifies roles and responsibilities and ensures we are meeting our legal requirements in these important areas. The right input We have a Developing Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Group who meet to discuss how we’re doing now, and what we could be doing better in the future. This group is open to all staff at all levels of the organisation and provides safe space to discuss ideas and improvements. The right standards In 2016, we were proud to achieve the Investors in Diversity Award and are continuing work to ensure we meet this standard on an ongoing basis. In 2020, we also celebrating 2 years as a Disability Confident Employer and ranked 65th in the National Centre for Diversity Awards. While we’re thrilled with these achievements, we know there’s lots of work still to do and areas that we could do better in. Cardiff Volunteering, collectively known in this notice as "The Students' Union", "Us" or "We" ( find out more about our corporate structure ), is committed to protecting the rights of our students, members & customers in line with the general data protection regulations. This page explains how your information is used, who it may be passed to and what your rights and responsibilities are. The three companies that make up our corporate structure are registered with the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) to process personal data and you can view the registration on the ICO's website under the Data Protection Register for CUSU, Data Protection Register for CUSL , and Data Protection Register for CV . This notice may be updated from time to time to ensure continued compliance with current legislation and to reflect best practice. Cardiff University Students' Union is registered in Wales. Company Registration No. 07328777. Charity No. 1137163 Purposes Current students of Cardiff University The Students' Union will receive an up to date copy of your student record directly from Cardiff University (unless you have opted out of Students' Union membership at enrolment), from the start of your enrolment to the end of your course your information will be stored on our secure servers.
You can find out more about this transference of data by viewing the University Data Sharing Agreement .
The Students’ Union will notify all members when elections are running in line with Article 6 (e), for the purpose of carrying out fair elections the processing of Student data is necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in the exercise of official authority vested in the controller as is in our memorandum and Part 3 of Ordinance 13. Past students of Cardiff University As an alumni of Cardiff University you will be entitled to continue to use our services, your account will be automatically archived at the end of your studies for purposes of records of achievement and account transaction history management, if you wish to regain full access to the range of services at the end of your studies please send an email to us at [email protected] quoting “Alumni SU Account”. General public (our customers) The Students' Union will collect your personal data during your online application, we will continue to process your personal data so that we can manage our contractual obligations, fulfil our and your legitimate interests and satisfy our statutory responsibilities. Your personal data will be used to manage your online account - including memberships and entitlements; allow you to purchase and access stored event tickets; manage event entrances and guest lists; notify you of changes; provide services (food and drink provisions); carry out legal duties (including providing information to others - see disclosures section); use your data to produce anonymous demographics; use your contact details for the purpose of promotion and marketing where consent is first freely given. Personal information may be collected separately and in person or by any other means from staff of the organisation, such as our security personnel or events management for the purposes of public safety. Any information obtained will be GDPR compliant and if such an occurrence takes place an explanation of why and how the data will be used will be communicated. Mailchimp & Our Marketing Mailing Lists The Students' Union currently operates two Mailchimp subscriber mailing lists: With our Offers & Promotions Mailing List you can sign up to if you are interested in hearing all about our current and future events, any sweet deals and offers us or our partners might be running and our September activities. With our Cardiff Students Alumni Mailling List you can sign up if you are a graduate of Cardiff University and want to hear all about our Alumni events including our annual Varsity. We will use your consent to join these mailing lists, this is captured when you fill out either of the subscriber forms, If you opt into our marketing communications via OpenTable or our App you will be consenting to joining the Offers & Promotions Mailing List . We will never share your personal data with anyone without first getting your explicit consent to do so, we will keep you on the mailing list for two years before we will notify you to remind you that your data is still held by us for the purpose of sending you our marketing material. You can unsubscribe from either of these lists by click unsubscribe in any email you have received or by contacting [email protected] . Business to Business The Students' Union will keep a record of business contacts that “We” have or that have provided a service to “Us” in a business capacity, this information will be kept securely and will be processed lawfully in line with our legitimate interest to do so. The Students' Union will use this information to communicate business to business services and to fulfil contractual obligations. This information will be shared to comply with statutory requirements and for the purposes of audit. Disclosure The Students' Union may share your relevant personal data with the following bodies where we have a lawful basis to do so: Fulfil a contract where a contract exists with you. In accordance with the terms of the contract. The governing body for university sport in the United Kingdom (BUCS) In order to confirm entry into the British Universities and Colleges Sport competitions "we" will (on request) share information to process your application (BUCS DSA) University Hospital of Wales and/or South Wales police Where an individual is not capable of giving consent and we have a duty to protect their vital interest. Work placement sites or educational partners involved in joint course provision. Where this is necessary for the delivery of your programme of study. Potential employers or providers of education whom you have approached To confirm your qualifications, references or development courses. UK agencies with duties relating to the prevention and detection of crime, collection of a tax or duty or safeguarding national security In order to allow the assessment, and payment and collection of relevant taxes i.e Council Tax, and benefits. To aid the police, UK Visas and Immigration Agency or the Foreign and Commonwealth Office. (This happens only as necessary and in consideration of your rights and freedoms) Jobshop In accordance with the University and Students' Union Data Sharing Agreement and with your consent where an application is made to use the Jobshop service ( Jobshop Sharing Agreements ). You can view the Jobshop Recruitment & Selection Privacy Notice here. Cardiff Student Letting In accordance with the University and Students' Union; Data Sharing Agreement and with your consent or where an application is made or a contract or tenancy agreement is in place. ( Download and View Cardiff Student Letting Privacy Notice ) Any other disclosures that the Students’ Union makes will be in accordance with a lawful basis defined in the UK General Data Protection Regulations and your interests will always be considered. Website Analytics We use Matomo , a privacy-focused analytics platform, to understand how students and visitors interact with our website. This helps us improve content, navigation, and the overall user experience — without compromising your privacy. We've set Matomo up to protect your privacy: No Cookies – Matomo runs in cookieless mode. No Personal Data – We don’t track anything that can identify you. Anonymised IPs – Your IP address is anonymised and can’t be linked back to you. Data Ownership – All analytics data is stored securely on our own servers in the UK and is never shared with third parties. How long your information will be held The Students' Union will retain your personal information for different periods of time depending on the services you have used and if you are a student, alumni or customer. Your transaction history will be kept for 7 years from the date of transaction. Ticket event attendance lists are kept for 2 years from the date of the event. Your online account will be kept open indefinitely unless you have asked “Us” to close it or if we have taken the decision to do so. As a training provider the Students’ Union will keep a student record of any studies that you have undertaken with “Us” permanently. This student record will include, name, date of birth, course attended, date of course and any grades obtained. Security of your information UK General Data Protection Regulations require us to keep your information secure. This means that your confidentiality will be respected, and all appropriate measures will be taken to prevent unauthorised access and disclosure. Only members of staff who need access to relevant personal data will be authorised to do so. Information about you in electronic form will be subject to password and other security restrictions, while paper files will be stored in secure areas with controlled access. Some processing may be undertaken on behalf of the Students’ Union by an organisation contracted for that purpose. Organisations processing personal data on behalf of the Students’ Union will be bound by an obligation to process personal data in accordance with Data Protection legislation. Your rights You have a right to access your personal information through the a Subject Access Request, You also have a right to object to the processing of your personal information, to rectify, to erase, to restrict and to port your personal information.  Any requests or objections should be made in writing to the Data Protection Officer using the contact details provided below. Your responsibilities You have a responsibility to keep your personal details up to date, as a student you can do so via SIMS , as a member of the public you can do so by either logging into your profile management on the website or by contacting [email protected] How to raise a query, concern or complaint If after reading this page you still have queries, concerns or wish to raise a complaint you should contact the Data Protection Officer in the first instance at the following: Data Protection Officer Cardiff University Students’ Union University Union Park Place Cardiff CF10 3QN Email: [email protected] Tel: 029 2078 1405 If you remain dissatisfied then you have the right to apply directly to the Information Commissioner for investigation. staff. As an organisation located in Cymru and based in the capital city, it’s an integral part of all that we offer and ensuring that students and customers have access to their language of choice is a priority for us. Our Welsh development plan During the 2023/24 academic year, this development plan was prepared with support from the Welsh Language Commissioner’s Tîm Hybu and in May 2024, we are pleased to have received Cynnig Cymraeg accreditation. This award is given to organisations who have a strong Welsh Language development plan, and we're delighted we're the first SU in Wales to receive one. Through the development of this plan, we are strengthening our commitment to the Welsh Language and setting out our future aspirations. This academic year also saw the introduction of a new elected Vice President Welsh Language, Community and Culture who represents all those who use Cymraeg within the Union, University and beyond. Our full Welsh Language Policy can be found here , and we are in the process of reviewing the policy as part of renewed commitment to Cymraeg within the Union. Welsh Development Plan Yn Undeb Myfyrwyr Caerdydd rydym yn cydnabod pwysigrwydd y Gymraeg i'n myfyrwyr a staff. Fel sefydliad wedi'i leoli ym mhrifddinas Cymru, mae'n rhan annatod o'r hyn rydym yn ei gynnig, ac mae sicrhau bod gan fyfyrwyr a chwsmeriaid fynediad at eu hiaith o ddewis yn flaenoriaeth i ni. Ein Cynllun Datblygu'r Gymraeg Yn ystod y flwyddyn academaidd 2023/24, paratowyd y cynllun datblygu yma gyda chefnogaeth gan Dîm Hybu Comisiynydd y Gymraeg , ac ym Mai 2024 mae'n bleser cyhoeddi ein bod wedi derbyn achrediad y Cynnig Cymraeg. Mae'r achrediad yma'n cydnabod sefydliadau gyda chynllun datblygu'r Gymraeg cryf, ac rydym yn falch iawn mai ni yw'r UM cyntaf yng Nghymru i'w dderbyn. Questions Sesiwn RGA Cyflwyno eich Sesiwn RGA Gwirfoddoli Helpwch Wneud RGA yn Wych Cwestiynau Cyffredin a T&A Cwestiynau Cyffredin Welcome to Give it a Go, where you can new things and uncovering the endless possibilities of university life. Whether you're a fresher looking to dive headfirst into the university experience, or a seasoned student seeking something new, Give it a Go has got you covered! Our programme is broken down in to two types of events: those organised by our amazing student groups, such as our sports clubs and societies and exciting experiences planned by the SU ourselves. When it comes to the SU's Give it a Go sessions, get packed and ready to embark on epic journeys across the United Kingdom. We've got an incredible range of trips lined up, from exploring the mysterious wonders of Stonehenge to immersing yourself in the intellectual location of Oxford and walking the breath-taking Jurassic Coast. But we don't stop there! We'll even whisk you away to the impressive city of Edinburgh or to rural North Wales. And the best part? We've made it all incredibly affordable, with student-friendly prices that won't break the bank. Now, let's talk about our student groups. Brace yourself for a multitude of opportunities, all curated by our exceptional students. Whatever your passion or curiosity, we've got something that satisfy your urge to explore and make memories. From football to ultimate frisbee, we've got the perfect outlet for your competitive spirit. Or get ready to explore cultural societies that celebrate diversity and connect you with students from across the world. Got a particular passion? From anime to art, baking to belly dance, chemistry to creative writing, there’s something for you! But what sets our Give it a Go sessions apart is the chance to "try before you buy." We understand that commitment can be daunting, so we offer you the opportunity to meet the society, experience their magic first-hand, and truly get a taste of what they have to offer. It's the ultimate test-drive before making your decision. So, seize the moment, dive into new experiences, and let Give it a Go be your passport to an extraordinary university journey. Let curiosity guide you, friendships flourish, and memories stay with you for life. The adventure awaits – are you ready to Give it a Go? Croeso i Rho Gynnig Arni lle gallwch brofi pethau newydd a darganfod y cyfleoedd diddiwedd sydd ar gael tra yn y brifysgol. Boed os ydych yn glas-fyfyriwr sy’n awyddus i gymryd rhan ymhob agwedd o fywyd prifysgol, neu’n fyfyriwr hŷn yn edrych am rywbeth newydd, mae Rho Gynnig Arni yma i’ch helpu! Mae ein rhaglen wedi’i rhannu’n ddau fath: rheiny wedi’u trefnu gan ein grwpiau myfyrwyr anhygoel, megis ein clybiau chwaraeon a chymdeithasau, a phrofiadau wedi’u trefnu gan yr UM. Pan mae’n dod i sesiynau Rho Gynnig Arni yr UM, byddwch yn barod i bacio’ch bag a mynd ar deithiau epig ar draws y Deyrnas Unedig. Mae gennym ystod anhygoel o deithiau ar y gweill, o weld Côr y Cewri i fwynhau dinas osgeiddig Rhydychen a cherdded ar hyd yr Arfordir Jwrasig. Ac mae mwy! Byddwn hefyd yn mynd ar deithiau hirach i Gaeredin a chefn gwlad Gogledd Cymru. A’r rhan gorau? Rydym wedi’u gwneud yn fforddiadwy, gyda phrisiau sy’n addas i chi fel myfyrwyr. Nawr, gadewch i ni drafod ein grwpiau myfyrwyr. Paratowch am amrywiaeth o gyfleoedd wedi’u trefnu gan ein myfyrwyr rhagorol. Beth bynnag yw’ch diddordeb, mae gennym rywbeth i chi. O bêl-droed i ffrisbi, mae yna chwaraeon di-ri i chi droi eich llaw at. Neu cymerwch ran mewn cyfleoedd gyda chymdeithasau diwylliannol sy’n dathlu amrywiaeth ac yn cysylltu myfyrwyr o ar draws y byd. Os oes gennych ddiddordeb penodol o anime i actio, hoci i hanes, jazz i japaneeg, mae yna rywbeth i chi! Ond beth sy’n gwneud ein sesiynau Rho Gynnig Arni yn unigryw? Rydym yn deall y gall ymrwymiad fod ychydig yn frawychus, felly rydym yn cynnig cyfle i gwrdd â chymdeithasau, profi eu gweithgareddau, a gwir cael blas ar yr hyn maent yn ei gynnig, cyn i chi benderfynu ymaelodi. Joining a Society or committee at Cardiff University Students' Union will guarantee that your time in Cardiff is unforgettable! With over 200 Societies to choose from, there's something to suit everyone. Any questions? Come and see us on the 3rd floor of the Students' Union or contact [email protected] . Can't find the Society for you? You could bring back an inactive society from our Save A Society list. Or why not set up your own Society? You can find our more about starting a Society here . Society memberships are available throughout the academic year so it's never too late to join any of our Societies. To be able to sign up for a membership, you need to join the Guild of Societies first. You can find out more about the Guild and how to join right here ! Non-Cardiff University students can apply to join Societies as an Associate Member by completing this online form . Each programme across the university has Student Academic Reps, who are elected to represent their cohort on educational matters. Do you have some feedback and want to know who your Student Academic Rep is? Click the Find my Rep button below to find and contact your Student Rep. You will need to log in to use Find my Rep. Os hoffech drafod unrhyw agweddau ar y rôl gyda thîm Llais y Myfyrwyr, cysylltwch â [email protected] . What is a Student Academic Representative? Beth yw Cynrychiolydd Academaidd Myfyrwyr? Every programme has a Student Academic Rep to represent the views of their cohort. Within the 24 schools at Cardiff University, this means over 1000 Reps every year across the organisation. Reps bridge the gap between students and staff members, gathering relevant feedback, raising it at meetings, and reporting back on any outcomes. Mae gan bob rhaglen Gynrychiolydd Academaidd Myfyrwyr i gynrychioli barn eu carfan. O fewn 24 ysgol ym Mhrifysgol Caerdydd, mae hyn yn golygu dros 1000 o Gynrychiolwyr ar draws y sefydliad bob blwyddyn. Mae cynrychiolwyr yn pontio’r bwlch rhwng myfyrwyr ac aelodau staff, gan gasglu adborth perthnasol, ei godi mewn cyfarfodydd, ac adrodd yn ôl ar unrhyw ganlyniadau. What types of issues do Student Academic Reps deal with? Pa fathau o faterion y mae Cynrychiolwyr Academaidd Myfyrwyr yn delio â nhw? Student Academic Reps are elected to speak on behalf of their cohorts’ educational concerns. This means they deal with issues or problems that arise regarding the course (including assessments and feedback, module content, or timetabling). They are not expected to deal with any wellbeing concerns or personal matters relating to students on their course. However, they will be able to signpost students with such concerns to appropriate university services. Mae Cynrychiolwyr Academaidd Myfyrwyr yn cael eu hethol i siarad ar ran pryderon addysgol eu carfannau. Mae hyn yn golygu eu bod yn delio â materion neu broblemau sy’n codi ynghylch y cwrs (gan gynnwys asesiadau ac adborth, cynnwys modiwlau, neu amserlennu). Nid oes disgwyl iddynt ddelio ag unrhyw bryderon lles na materion personol sy’n ymwneud â myfyrwyr ar eu cwrs. Fodd bynnag, byddant yn gallu cyfeirio myfyrwyr sydd â phryderon o'r fath at wasanaethau prifysgol priodol. How do I find the Student Academic Rep for my school? Sut mae dod o hyd i’r Cynrychiolydd Academaidd Myfyrwyr ar gyfer fy ysgol? Your Student Academic Rep should make themselves known to you in the first few weeks of the year. You can also find the details of your Rep by filtering by your college, school, and year in the Find My Rep widget above. I ble mae adborth yn mynd? The university has a comprehensive committee structure that is designed to ensure that all feedback can be resolved or discussed at the appropriate level. Any feedback that is passed onto Student Academic Representatives will be raised with school staff at a Student Staff Panel meeting. Depending on the nature of the issue, the panel of staff and students may find a solution, which will then be communicated back to students. If no solution can be found, the issue will be allocated to another appropriate committee, who will work towards an outcome. Mae gan y brifysgol strwythur pwyllgor cynhwysfawr sydd wedi’i gynllunio i sicrhau y gellir datrys neu drafod yr holl adborth ar y lefel briodol. Os na ellir dod o hyd i ateb, bydd y mater yn cael ei ddyrannu i bwyllgor priodol arall, a fydd yn gweithio tuag at ganlyniad. What is a Student Staff Panel? Beth yw Panel Staff Myfyrwyr? Student Staff Panels are meetings that occur between Student Academic Representatives and staff within the school. These happen once per semester and exist to ensure that there is an effective dialogue between staff and students. These are led by a student Chair and Vice-Chair, and facilitation is supported by school staff. Any outcomes from Student Staff Panel meetings should be communicated with all students. What is a College Forum? Beth yw Fforwm Coleg? College Forums are meetings facilitated by the Students’ Union and provide an opportunity for Reps to report issues that cannot be resolved at a Student Staff Panel. These are split by college and are chaired by a Sabbatical Officer. The Chair and Vice-Chair of each Student Staff Panel will be invited to attend and provide an update on the items discussed at their latest meeting. College Deans and professional service staff will also be in attendance, so if there is any feedback that is not suitable for a Student Staff Panel, it can be raised at a College Forum. Why should I volunteer Pam ddylwn i wirfoddoli? Becoming a Student Academic Representative is a great opportunity. Not only can you represent your cohort and gain an insight into the workings of your school, you will also gain lots of transferable skills that will look great on your CV. As a Rep, you will receive regular communication from the Students’ Union with additional opportunities. You can also get a certificate at the end of the year! Fel cynrychiolydd, byddwch yn derbyn cyfathrebiad rheolaidd gan Undeb y Myfyrwyr gyda chyfleoedd ychwanegol. Gallwch hefyd gael tystysgrif ar ddiwedd y flwyddyn! Will I receive training and support? A fydda i’n derbyn hyfforddiant a chefnogaeth? As a Student Academic Representative, you will receive comprehensive training from the Student Voice team about your role. This will take you through what to expect from your role, and the support you can access. You will also receive an induction from the Student Rep Coordinator within your school, who will give you information about how you can communicate with staff and students, and what you may need to consider when providing feedback. At the end of the year, every Student Academic Rep who completed training can claim a certificate as evidence of the skills they have gained throughout the role. selection: Yes Current selection: Yes Current selection: Yes Current selection: Yes The Annual General Meeting (AGM) is a large forum where a wide variety of students come to debate and determine the direction of the Students’ Union. The AGM usually takes place at the end of November, and we use the AGM to adopt a collective stance on an issue and decide what action the Students’ Union will take. Mae’r Cyfarfod Cyffredinol Blynyddol (CCB) yn fforwm mawr lle mae amrywiaeth eang o fyfyrwyr yn dod i drafod a phenderfynu ar gyfeiriad Undeb y Myfyrwyr. Fel arfer, cynhelir y CCB ddiwedd mis Tachwedd, ac rydym yn defnyddio’r CCB i fabwysiadu safbwynt ar y cyd ar fater a phenderfynu pa gamau y bydd Undeb y Myfyrwyr yn eu cymryd. Notice of AGM Hysbysiad o’r CCB The Students’ Union hereby gives notice that the Student Members’ Annual General Meeting (AGM) will take place at 18:00 on Thursday 20 November 2025. Mae Undeb y Myfyrwyr yn eich hysbysu y bydd Cyfarfod Cyffredinol Blynyddol (CCB) yr Aelodau yn cael ei gynnal am 18:00 dydd Iau 20 Tachwedd 2025. The meeting will be held in the Great Hall on the first floor of the Students’ Union at 18:00. Doors will open at 17.30. Every student at Cardiff University is invited and encouraged to attend. Just remember to bring your Student ID card as it will be required on entry. Bydd y cyfarfod yn cael ei gynnal yn y Neuadd Fawr ar lawr cyntaf Undeb y Myfyrwyr am 18:00. Agenda Submit Questions to Trustees Read our Annual Impact Report 2024-25 What is the AGM? Beth yw CCB? It is a large forum where a wide variety of students come to debate and determine the direction of Cardiff Students’ Union. Mae’n fforwm mawr lle mae amrywiaeth eang o fyfyrwyr yn dod i drafod a phenderfynu ar gyfeiriad Undeb Myfyrwyr Caerdydd. Any student can attend the AGM and have their say on the items discussed. The Union is a transparent organisation which is run by the student population. This is a great opportunity to have a hands-on impact on the democracy and running of the Students’ Union. Gall unrhyw fyfyriwr fynychu’r Cyfarfod Cyffredinol Blynyddol a dweud eu dweud ar yr eitemau a drafodir. Mae’r Undeb yn sefydliad tryloyw sy’n cael ei redeg gan boblogaeth y myfyrwyr. Mae hwn yn gyfle gwych i gael effaith go iawn ar ddemocratiaeth a’r ffordd y caiff Undeb y Myfyrwyr ei rhedeg. In unusual circumstances when an urgent decision needs to be made, an Extraordinary General Meeting may also be called at another point in the year.
